headline: WARSH GOES HAWKISH AT JACKSON HOLE — Gold Falls 1.2% as New Fed Chair Warns Inflation Fight 'Has Work to Do'
snippet: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivered a hawkish debut at Jackson Hole, warning that inflation is not decelerating fast enough and the Fed 'has work to do.' The dollar surged in response, sending spot gold down 1.2% to ~$4,603/oz — pulling back from multi-day highs near $4,650 reached earlier Friday.

headline: GOLD MINERS MAKE HISTORY — MSCI Global Index Up 43% in August, Biggest Monthly Gain on Record
snippet: The MSCI global gold miners index has surged 43% in August — on track for its biggest monthly gain in recorded history — as gold's 13% rise above $4,500/oz drives outsized earnings leverage across producers. The gain dwarfs the semiconductor sector's own best recent month of 38% (PHLX Index, April 2026).

headline: SIBANYE, HARMONY SURGE 48% — South Africa's Mining Index Rockets 38% in August, Best Month in Bloomberg History
snippet: The FTSE/JSE Precious Metals and Mining Total Return Index has jumped 38% in August — the largest monthly gain in Bloomberg data going back to 2006 — erasing a year-to-date loss of roughly 20%. AngloGold Ashanti, Pan African Resources and Gold Fields each climbed more than 40%, while Harmony Gold and Sibanye Stillwater led the index at +48%.

headline: WESTGOLD POSTS RECORD FY26 — 41% Ore Reserve Jump to 4.1Moz at $27/oz Cost; Cash Flow and Treasury Hit All-Time Highs
snippet: Westgold Resources (ASX/TSX: WGX) reported record full-year 2026 results, with gold price tailwinds driving record earnings, cash flow and treasury growth. Ore Reserves grew 41% to 4.1Moz at a reserve addition cost of just $27/oz, while the Ore Reserve grade improved 15% and Mineral Resources grew 8% to 14.4Moz.

headline: USAR SURGES FRIDAY ON DOE GRANTS — Critical Minerals Sector Catches Broad Bid as Hard Asset Rotation Accelerates
snippet: USA Rare Earth (USAR) surged Friday as the DOE's $500 million critical minerals grant program and the company's Serra Verde shareholder vote drove sector-wide buying. MP Materials climbed 5%, REMX jumped 6%, with analysts citing 30-year Treasury yields at 2007 highs as capital rotates into scarce hard assets.

headline: CRITICAL METALS SPIKES 19% AS EUROPEAN LITHIUM MERGER ENTERS FINAL STRETCH — Greenland Rare Earths Vote Imminent
snippet: Critical Metals Corp (CRML) spiked 19% as European Lithium shareholders prepare to vote on an $835 million tie-up that would combine European Lithium's Czech lithium assets with Critical Metals' majority-owned Tanbreez rare earths project in Greenland. The companies amended the share scheme to a floating ratio ahead of the late-August vote.

headline: FREEPORT BACKS FINLAY MINERALS TO 4,400m — PIL Program Expands 57% at British Columbia Copper-Gold Target
snippet: Finlay Minerals (TSX-V: FYL) has expanded its 2026 PIL Property drill program to 4,400 metres — up from 2,800m — with the additional 1,600m fully funded by Freeport-McMoRan under an earn-in agreement. Over 2,700m has been drilled at the Gold and Reef targets adjacent to Freeport and Amarc's JOY copper-gold project in BC.

headline: PROSPECTIVA RESOURCES SPUDS MAIDEN DRILL AT SÃO FRANCISCO — 2,500m, 10-Hole Copper-Gold Program Underway in Brazil
snippet: Prospectiva Resources (TSX-V: PSVA) has commenced its fully funded maiden diamond drill program at the São Francisco Copper-Gold Project in Brazil, comprising 2,500 metres across 10 holes to test a high-priority copper-gold porphyry target.

headline: CANSTAR DRILLS WIDEST-EVER SULPHIDE AT MARY MARCH — 15.6m @ 2.3% CuEq Including 9.75m @ 3.3% from 467m Depth
snippet: Canstar Resources (TSX-V: ROX) reported the widest massive sulphide intercept in the Mary March Project's drilling record from its first 2026 holes at the Buchans district VMS target in Newfoundland. Drill hole MM-26-42 returned 15.6 metres grading 2.3% copper equivalent from 467.4m depth, including 9.75m at 3.3% CuEq.

headline: FISCAL FEAR TRADE DRIVES MINERS HIGHER EVEN AS GOLD SLIPS — $40 Trillion US Debt Load Is Structural Bull Case
snippet: Gold mining equities including Agnico Eagle (+2%), Newmont (+2.2%) and Barrick Mining (+2.1%) extended their August rally even as spot gold slipped — a decoupling analysts attribute to the fiscal fear trade, as US debt above $40 trillion and a near-$2 trillion annual deficit drive institutional capital into miners as a structural inflation hedge.
